qualification: local A05.3 read-only multi-access target chaining measurement; not A05.3 closure, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.boundary: Each generated memory block publishes its own restartable-read policy before its first callback. Direct-chain and IBTC admission includes multi-access targets only when compiled metadata proves that the target does not write guest memory.
candidate.conservativeExclusions: Multi-access targets that may write guest memory remain dispatcher-separated after the all-target production soft-lock. Baseline targets with interpreter guards also remain excluded.
candidate.regressionCoverage: A callback-free source chains into a two-read target whose second access declines and recovers the exact two-block prefix. A load/store target is separately proven to retain two dispatcher entries and zero direct-chain bypasses. Both tests execute in baseline and tier-one modes.

verification.focused: Four replay-policy, target-admission, and ABI-layout tests passed.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,555 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the frozen fixture was executed explicitly.
verification.diffCheck: git diff --check passed before the focused implementation commit.

disposition.reason: Read-only multi-access targets improve normalized dispatcher entries by 8.46 percent over the accepted single-access target slice and pass the pinned production workload, but within-run avoidance remains far below the strict greater-than-95-percent gate. The card stays open.

limitations: This is one local measurement, sufficient to reject gate closure but not to make a stable wall-time comparison.
Retired instruction totals differ from the reference run, so normalized and within-run dispatcher ratios are reported instead of an unmatched raw-count claim.
Multi-access write, RMW, stack-memory, and guarded baseline targets remain dispatcher-separated.
